messages:
Maria: FYI saw a weird race between resource-tag propagation and telemetry fanout during a private->dedicated handoff. metrics are duplicated in the central sink and missing in the private sink for ~30s.
Aj: repro steps?
Maria: quick notes: create private deployment, switch to dedicated via UI, run load test. logs show requests hitting dedicated runtime before control-plane tags arrive. sample header we see from runtime:
```
X-RDWD-Res-ID: acct-12345
X-RDWD-Res-Ver: 834
X-RDWD-Telemetry-Route: private-sink
```
then control plane emits telemetry-config:update event about 10-30s later.
Leo: sounds like a classic eventual-consistency fanout race. When runtime routes telemetry it uses local cache mapping (res-id->sink). If that map is stale you either drop or double-send depending on fallback.
Sophie: two problems: correctness (missing/duplicated metrics) and data governance — private sink must get data, central should not get private data. any temporary misrouting is bad.
Nate: options: 1) Synchronous registration: block first requests until CP ack of tag mapping (adds ~50-200ms) 2) Enforce forward-only routing: if no mapping, buffer locally and reconcile (adds complexity + storage) 3) Versioned handshake: control plane pushes manifest with a monotonic `res-ver`; runtime only routes when seen version >= manifest version 4) Sidecar-local authoritative override: sidecar accepts ephemeral mapping and marks telemetry as sensitive until CP ack
Aj: tradeoffs: (1) is simple but increases tail latency for the first request, (2) is complex operationally, (3) needs a robust versioning system and failure modes, (4) requires extra surface for sidecar ownership.
Maria: we saw ~60s windows in worst case on prod during a rollout which caused alerts. I prefer a small sync step on creation/switch and then eventual model for subsequent ops.
Leo: implementation sketch for versioned handshake:
```
control-plane: publish manifest {res_id: acct-12345, res_ver: 834, sinks: ["private-sink"], ts: 1712233445}
runtime: subscribe to manifest stream, apply when res_ver > local.
runtime routing: if local_res_ver < manifest_res_ver -> hold telemetry in memory queue (max 1s), if still stale -> drop and emit debug metric
```
Sophie: holding in memory + 1s fallback still risks leakage. we need a hard policy: if resource is marked `private` in the manifest, never fanout to central unless CP explicitly allows. so default safe-fail = route to private only or drop.
Aj: that implies runtime needs to know privacy semantics before routing — i.e., manifest must be pushed before runtime accepts production traffic for that customer. which is the sync step Maria suggested.
Nate: alternative: attach a `privacy-tag` in the routing header from the client (P0: risky), or a short-lived `probe` request to force control-plane realization. probe would be cheap and give CP chance to reconcile.
Maria: probe idea is nice: on handoff, control-plane returns `200 probe-id` to the operator UI and pushes manifest; runtime on first traffic sees probe header `X-RDWD-Probe: <id>` and blocks routing until it matches.
Sophie: ok but failure scenarios: if CP is partitioned, we must avoid blocking forever. add a timeout (e.g., 5s) and fall back to safe route (private-only) + emit alert.
Leo: action items:
- Aj: prototype manifest + runtime subscriber (small prototype in eng-runtime). keep message size small.
- Maria: add regression test that simulates CP delay and asserts no central-sink leakage.
- Nate: draft telemetry policy: safe-fail semantics + timeouts + metrics.
- Sophie: write audit checklist for sensitive sink migrations.
ops-bot: deploy-checker: new rollout rule added to CI: require manifest-publish ACK for private->dedicated transitions in staging.
Aj: also we should add per-resource monotonic version header: `X-RDWD-Res-Ver` so we can correlate logs and make postmortem easier.
Maria: agreed. final leaning: gated handoff (short sync + manifest publish) + runtime version checks + short in-memory hold window + safe-fail route to private-only after timeout.
Sophie: call this "gated manifest handshake" in docs. I'll add to the hosting-mode handoff RFC as a follow-up.
Nate: I'll spec the metrics we need: `telemetry.fanout.attempts`, `telemetry.fanout.drops`, `manifest.apply.latency`, `manifest.missing.timeouts` and an alert when `fanout.drops > 0` for private resources.
Maria: cool. timeline? small prototype this week, tests next sprint.
Aj: ping me when prototype ready, I'll review.
Maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
